description: Cosmic Ray 64 is a software developers dedicated to solving complex problems through code and algorithms. For this NASA challenge, we are developing a health monitoring platform that turns a simple cam into a clinical tool. We focus on the early detection of deep cognitive fatigue and sleep deprivation by analyzing blink patterns and eye movements. Our software operates locally to ensure rapid diagnostics without relying on an internet connection.
summary:
Cosmic Ray 64 is a crew wellbeing and mission-support web application designed for long-duration space missions and communication delays with Earth.

The application helps crews record and review sleep, mood, stress, fatigue, symptoms, reaction time, and manually measured vital signs. It organizes personal records by crew member and date, allowing users to observe changes over time without presenting the information as a medical diagnosis.

The platform also includes mission-risk scenarios based on NASA’s human spaceflight hazards, a Mars communication-delay simulation, EVA preparation using NOAA space-weather observations, emergency coordination tools, shift handover reports, and local report preparation.

Cosmic Ray 64 is designed to support crew autonomy, improve traceability, and help astronauts organize information while waiting for communication with Earth. It is an educational support prototype and does not replace medical personnel, approved mission procedures, or operational authorization.
details:
PROJECT OVERVIEW

Cosmic Ray 64 is a bilingual React and TypeScript web application that supports crew wellbeing tracking and mission coordination during long-duration space missions.

CREW WELLBEING TRACKING

Users can select a crew profile and record:

  • Sleep
  • Mood
  • Perceived stress
  • Fatigue
  • Symptoms and optional notes
  • Reaction time
  • Manually measured vital signs

Records are stored locally by crew member and date using browser localStorage.

PERSONAL TRENDS AND COGNITION

The overview presents personal trends and radar visualizations for comparing daily records. The application does not calculate a clinical health score, diagnose conditions, or replace medical evaluation. Missing information remains unmeasured instead of being replaced with invented values.

The cognition section includes a visual reaction-time test based on the user’s response to a visual cue.

MISSION CONTEXT

Cosmic Ray 64 includes mission-risk scenarios for:

  • Earth orbit
  • Lunar missions
  • Mars transit
  • Extravehicular activity

These scenarios are organized around NASA’s five human spaceflight hazards and are presented as educational context.

MARS COMMUNICATION-DELAY SIMULATION

Mars mode provides:

  • An illustrative communication-delay simulation
  • Shift coordination
  • Task tracking
  • A mission log
  • A downloadable report

The simulation is local and illustrative. It does not connect to Earth or calculate the current position of the planets.

EVA PREPARATION AND NOAA OBSERVATIONS

The EVA preparation section displays NOAA space-weather observations and allows users to document preparation plans. These observations do not estimate personal radiation dose or authorize an EVA.

EMERGENCY COORDINATION

The emergency section supports:

  • Emergency category selection
  • Event timing
  • Observations
  • Assigned roles
  • Coordination checklists
  • Notes
  • Local report preparation
  • Downloadable records

Reports remain local and are not transmitted to Earth. The application does not generate medical treatment instructions.

TECHNOLOGY AND DEPLOYMENT

The application was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Recharts, and browser localStorage. It is hosted through Azure Static Web Apps and published from the project’s GitHub repository.
